competencies.text: Explain common reaction types: decomposition, acid on carbonates, acids on metals, combustion.
Identify reaction types in daily activities: baking, cleaning, burning.

days.title: Chemical Reactions Around Us
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to identify and describe four common types of chemical reactions that occur in your daily life: decomposition, acid on carbonates, acids on metals, and combustion.

🔬 What Is a Chemical Reaction?

A chemical reaction is a process where one or more substances (called reactants) change into new substances (called products). The atoms are rearranged — not created or destroyed — during the reaction.

Reactants → Products

🧪 Signs a Chemical Reaction Has Occurred

  • Gas bubbles — fizzing when you open soda
  • Color change — rust forming on iron
  • Temperature change — cooking releases heat
  • Precipitate forms — solid appears in a clear liquid
  • Light emitted — burning wood or fireworks
  • New odor — milk spoiling

⚗️ Four Common Reaction Types

Reaction TypeWhat HappensEveryday Example
DecompositionOne compound breaks down into two or more simpler substancesHydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) breaking into water and oxygen when used as an antiseptic
Acid on CarbonatesAn acid reacts with a carbonate → produces CO₂ gas, water, and a saltVinegar on baking soda producing fizz in cakes and volcano experiments
Acids on MetalsAn acid reacts with a metal → produces hydrogen gas and a saltDilute hydrochloric acid cleaning a rusty nail; lemon juice on aluminum foil
CombustionA substance reacts with oxygen → releases heat and lightBurning wood, LPG stove flame, jeepney engine, candles

🍰 Reaction Types in Daily Activities

  • Baking: Baking soda + vinegar (or acid in buttermilk) → CO₂ makes the cake rise. Acid on carbonate.
  • Cleaning: Bleach (NaClO) decomposes over time releasing oxygen — that's why old bleach is weaker. Decomposition.
  • Burning: LPG (C₃H₈) + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O + heat. Combustion.
  • Cooking in kalamansi juice: Citric acid + iron from fish → tenderizes. Acid on metal.
  • Rusting: Iron + oxygen + water → iron oxide (rust). Oxidation (slow combustion).

💡 Why This Matters

Understanding reaction types helps you:

  • Cook safely — know when to expect fizzing or heat.
  • Clean efficiently — pick the right chemical for the right mess.
  • Prevent accidents — never mix bleach with ammonia (acid-base reaction producing toxic gas).
  • Understand nature — from photosynthesis to rust, reactions drive everything.

📌 Quick Check

  • What type of reaction produces CO₂ when vinegar meets baking soda? (Answer: acid on carbonate)
  • Why does old bleach become weaker over time? (Answer: decomposition of NaClO)
  • What are the products of combustion of LPG? (Answer: CO₂ and H₂O plus heat)

days.title: Match Game — Reaction Types
days.content:
🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each reaction type or everyday scenario to its correct description. There are 8 pairs and unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

match.right: One compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances
Produces CO₂ gas, water, and a salt — like vinegar on baking soda
Produces hydrogen gas and a salt — like lemon juice on aluminum
Reaction with oxygen releasing heat and light — like burning LPG
Plants use CO₂ + H₂O + sunlight to make glucose and O₂
Slow oxidation of iron in the presence of oxygen and water
Cells break down glucose with O₂ to release energy
Acid + bicarbonate produces CO₂ to make cakes rise

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Reactions at Home
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: 🍰 Your mother bakes a cake and adds baking powder. When the cake is in the oven, it rises. What type of reaction is happening?

choices.label: B) Acid on carbonate — CO₂ gas is released, making the batter rise

scenario.text: 🔦 Your grandmother uses hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) on a wound. She notices fizzing. What happened?

choices.label: B) Decomposition — H₂O₂ breaks into water and oxygen gas, producing fizzing

scenario.text: 🚗 A jeepney burns diesel fuel to move. What are the products of this combustion reaction?

choices.label: A) Carbon dioxide, water vapor, and heat

scenario.text: 🔩 You spray a rusty gate with a cleaner containing phosphoric acid. The rust disappears, and bubbles form. What reaction type is this?

choices.label: C) Acid on metal — the acid reacts with iron oxide, producing a salt and hydrogen gas

scenario.text: ⚠️ You are told never to mix bleach with ammonia cleaner. What dangerous reaction happens if you do?

choices.label: A) Nothing — they are safe to mix
B) Toxic chloramine gas is released, which can damage lungs
C) It becomes a stronger bleach

days.title: Formative Check — Escape the Chem Lab
days.content:
🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Chem Lab

You have 3 lives and 6 keys to unlock. You need 75% (5 of 6) to pass. Take your time — read every option carefully.

escape.text: Which of the following BEST describes a chemical reaction?

choices.label: A) A physical change like melting ice
B) A process where reactants change into new products with different properties
C) A change in shape only
D) A change in temperature only

escape.text: What type of reaction occurs when vinegar is added to baking soda?
Why do we see bubbles when hydrogen peroxide is poured on a wound?

choices.label: B) H₂O₂ decomposes into water and oxygen gas
C) It is reacting with metal in the skin

escape.text: Which of the following is NOT a sign of a chemical reaction?

choices.label: C) Change in shape without any other change
D) Release of light or heat

escape.text: What are the products of complete combustion of a hydrocarbon fuel like LPG?
Why should you NEVER mix bleach with ammonia cleaner?

choices.label: A) It releases toxic chloramine gas that can damage your lungs
C) It loses all cleaning power
